Show the system window (auto request, fall back if denied)
Modal (intercept outside touches / above a Dialog)
The three pages below are companion scenarios for the app-level window; they are also reachable from the App-level global window page.
The same three windows written once more with the Java builders (JavaDemo.java), checking how Java-friendly the public API is.
Java: scoped window on this page (tag=%1$s)
Created %1$s (destroyed when you leave this page)
safeArea (keep clear of system bars / notch)
Open the blacklisted page (the window disappears)
Open the immersive page (no status bar)
Manual: show a dialog, then request

In the Manual dialog: Open settings = proceed(), Use fallback = useFallback(), Cancel = deny(). deny() only gives up — even with a fallback configured the window stays at INSTALLED (recoverable with retryPermission()); only useFallback() really falls back.
Skip (no permission check, type decided by the customizer)
Skip never checks the permission: without it addView fails (see the Fx-system log); once the permission is granted, tap retryPermission() to recover.
Not a system window right now (it fell back to AppHost)

The customizer runs after the default LayoutParams, so type / flags / alpha and the rest can all be overridden. alpha 0.5 reinstalls with a minimal config; tap the install button above to get the default config back.
With touchable off the window gets FLAG_NOT_TOUCHABLE and every touch passes straight through to the app below.
Install a system window with an EditText
Tap the EditText to open the keyboard; Back dismisses the keyboard and does not trigger onBackPressed.

A system window only needs an application context, so a Service can install one too (#192). On API 33+ a foreground service still starts without the notification permission — only the notification stays invisible.

Deny the permission to watch the fallback: fallback(AppHost) is configured by default, so a denied window switches to the app-level implementation and keeps showing. Without a fallback it stays at INSTALLED, waiting for retryPermission().
The Manual strategy hands the decision to you: explain what the permission is for, then request it, fall back, or give up.
ViewGroup host: the window can only move inside this area

API 29+ cancels the window automatically when the page is destroyed; on older versions cancel it yourself in onDestroy (this page does both). The position is remembered with FxSpStorage and restored when you come back.
ScopeFragment calls fxScope().show() in onCreate, before its view exists, so the window has to wait for that view — exactly #244.
Add the Fragment (with a window inside)
Remove the Fragment (its window is cancelled)
detach the Fragment (view destroyed, window gone)
attach the Fragment (view rebuilt, window returns)
AFTER_LONG_PRESS (drag only after a long press, #222)
dragRegion limits where a drag may start (#165); touches outside the region go to the content as usual.
Only the header can start a drag
When the content holds a scrollable RecyclerView, who owns a vertical gesture:
AUTO (yield when the spot below can scroll, default)
PARENT (take over past the slop, the list cannot scroll)
CHILD (never take over, only the list scrolls)
With touchable off the window takes no touches at all (#243/#108) — tapping it is the same as tapping the page below.
onClick / onLongClick / onDragStart / onDragEnd from addListener:
(try tapping, long-pressing or dragging the window)
The anchor is the edge or corner the content hugs; when a drag ends, core converts the drop point back into an anchor (that is also what gets persisted).
Overflow is off by default: the content is kept inside the usable area. Turn on a direction and the window can be dragged past that side.
The anchor stays put when the size changes (#187): drag the window into a corner, then grow or shrink it — the edge it hugs never moves.
Once on, every anchor commit (drag end / moveTo / update{anchor}) is written; reading happens only when the window is created, so leave this page and come back to see it restored.
Cleared the saved portrait and landscape positions for %1$s
After a rotation the position is restored per orientation: the storage key is tag:orientation (1 = portrait, 2 = landscape), one entry each.
The two windows use different tags, so their config, persisted position and listeners are all independent.
Scoped windows (fxScope / FloatingX.create) never enter the registry, so controls() does not list them.
Installing the same tag again replaces the entry in the registry and cancels the old control right away (a terminal state — every later call throws).

Tap Show below first, then tap this button: while the window is showing the container swallows the tap (the counter holds and the window hides itself); once the window is hidden — or modal is off — touches pass through again and the counter goes up.

While on, interception only happens when the window is showing (touches outside it are swallowed and the button below is dead) and one outside tap hides the window; once hidden, or with modal off, touches pass through as usual.
modal (intercept outside touches + hide on outside tap)
A Dialog is its own Window, stacked above the Activity: to cover it, attach the floating window to the Dialog decorView.
Show a Dialog with a window on top
The Dlg window in the top-right corner is attached to this Dialog decorView; it can be dragged inside the Dialog and is cancelled when the Dialog closes.
Tap the window to count: count uses rememberSaveable, vm uses viewModel(), and the third line shows the live coordinates from positionFlow() and the state from stateFlow().
Cancelled; tapping Show rebuilds it (counters reset)
count survives a rotation (rememberSaveable runs on FxComposeOwner)
Open the second page: count and vm should hold
Open the blacklisted page: the window disappears, count holds after you return
The same compose content in a system window (tag=%1$s): the permission is requested automatically and it falls back to an app window when denied. It can be shown alongside the app-level one above.

The window follows you here and both count and vm should keep their values:\n- the container only changed parent view; FxComposeOwner belongs to the control and does not die with the page (#210);\n- if the composition was ever disposed, rememberSaveable values are brought back by the FxComposeContent bridge registry.
Keep tapping the window here; the number should carry on where it left off when you go back.
The window should follow you here without any animation: the container only changed parent view, so engine state, features and animations are untouched and the position is kept as a translation.
This page is blacklisted (matched through its parent BaseBlackActivity, #221), so the window is hidden; it comes back when you leave.
With safeArea on the window keeps out of the notch and navigation bar; turn it off and it can sit right on the screen edge.
It holds after dragging anywhere too: when a drag ends, core converts the drop point into the nearest anchor.
With the overlay permission granted the same case holds on the System-level window page: a system window moves the WindowManager x/y, and size changes are still recomputed from the anchor.
Across pages: open the second page and come back
Detach and re-attach: open the blacklisted page and come back

On the blacklisted page the container is detached (the owner drops to CREATED and the composition is disposed); on return it recomposes — count comes back from the bridge registry and vm is the very same instance.
Control group: only cancel destroys the owner, which clears the ViewModel, so the next Show gives you a brand new window.

DemoWindows.installApp registers the parent class:\n blacklist(BaseBlackActivity::class.java)\nBlackActivity is not registered itself, it only extends BaseBlackActivity — isInstance matching stops it all the same.
Open BlackActivity (a subclass; the window should disappear)
Expected: the window disappears on BlackActivity (the container is detached) and comes back on its own when you return.
Turn adsorption off (stays where you drop it)
With safeArea off the usable area covers the whole window, so the floater can rest on the status or navigation bar; overflow then lets it go beyond the usable area as well.
It is attached to the DecorView: the drag area is the whole window, status and navigation bars included (attach it to android.R.id.content and the content area clips it).
Tapping again replaces the old Fragment: the old fragment is destroyed, its window is cancelled automatically, and the new fragment builds a fresh one.

Press Back to dismiss the keyboard first
